Avid

AV-id -- two syllables, stress on the first syllable, AV. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Avid is eager or enthusiastic.

An avid crossword solver, Nana finishes the Sunday puzzle in ink.

Worked Example

Every Tuesday, Sam is at the shop when the new skateboard magazines arrive. He knows the release date of every deck, saves his allowance for wheels, and can happily talk bearings for an hour.

Sam is avid: constantly eager about his chosen interest. Avid is a habit, not a mood -- it describes an ongoing appetite for an activity (an avid reader, an avid collector), never a one-time emotional high.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

voracious: A voracious reader devours books in great gulps -- the word measures how much gets consumed, and it always suggests enormous quantity. Avid measures faithfulness instead: an avid reader returns happily week after week, whatever the size of the pile.

dedicated: Dedicated means putting in steady, disciplined effort toward a goal, whether or not you enjoy it. Avid is about appetite: an avid birder is out early because she loves it, not because duty demands it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

reluctant: unwilling and hesitant

uninterested: having no interest at all

Where it sits · how hard the appetite is to satisfy — eager → avid → insatiable

eager vs. avid: Eager is the lighter, weaker word -- anyone can be eager for Friday -- while avid describes an appetite that keeps coming back: an avid reader wants the next book, and the one after that.

insatiable vs. avid: Insatiable is the strongest: an avid collector is happily hungry for more, but an insatiable one can never be satisfied at all, no matter how much the shelves already hold.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — av-

root — av-: to crave, to long for (Latin avere)

suffix — -id

suffix — -id: having the quality of (Latin -idus)

Put it together

Put it together: Avid comes from Latin avidus, 'craving,' built on avere, 'to long for.' The appetite is baked into the word: an avid reader genuinely craves the next book, the next puzzle, the next early-morning hike.

Use the root in a new word: avarice

Use the root in a new word: avarice: In the fable, the king's avarice grows until he cannot enjoy a single coin he owns.

Root Check

Word Choice

Avid pairs with the doer of a hobby: an avid reader, hiker, birder, collector. It names steady, habitual eagerness -- not an emotional peak (that is elated) and not devotion to a team or cause (that is ardent). If the sentence is about how often someone happily shows up for an activity, avid is your word.
